notes: Possessory action and employment dispute over a municipal golf-course clubhouse concession; selectors matched generic 'possession of the premises' and eviction language, but no letting of a dwelling or rooms for pay is at issue.

holding_summary: Plaintiff, a lodger in defendant's lodging house, sued to recover the value of property allegedly lost from his room while he was away in Cuba. The court found plaintiff's account of his losses (including diamond rings and cash) implausible and unproven, and affirmed judgment for the defendant lodging-house keeper without reaching the legal question of innkeeper liability.

holding_summary: Plaintiff, a boarder in his step-father's leased house who had paid his board in full, sought to enjoin seizure of his piano and parlor set for rent owed by his step-father to the landlord. The court held that a boarder in leased premises is a sub-tenant whose own property is subject to seizure for the tenant's unpaid rent only to the extent the boarder himself is indebted to the tenant, and affirmed judgment protecting plaintiff's property.

quotes.text: a boarder who lives in the leased premises is a sub-tenant, to the extent at least that the property belonging to him and contained in the leased premises is subject to seizure for the rent due by the tenant, only in so far as he is himself indebted to the tenant.

notes: Divorce/separation-from-bed-and-board case concerning marital domicile; selector matched the phrase 'bed and board' as a legal term of art, not compensated occupancy or lodging.

City ordinance banning all business on a street (aimed at a dry-goods grocery) struck down as ultra vires and unreasonable; a general police-power/business-regulation case, not one regulating lodging or boarding houses.
Commercial storehouse lease dispute over damages from a neighbor's party-wall repairs; no lodging, boarding, or residential letting is involved.
Ferry-franchise infringement case concerning a police jury's exclusive right to license ferries/bridges; unrelated to letting of dwellings or rooms despite matches on licensing/toll language.
Ordinary landlord-tenant holdover-rent suit; lessee sublet the upper floor and failed to surrender full possession at lease end. No boarding/lodging arrangement or its regulation is at issue.
Material man's lien suit over lumber used in construction of two buildings; no letting or lodging arrangement at issue.

Premises-liability suit by a woman injured falling through a skylight in a multi-unit apartment house; the case turns entirely on trespasser/attractive-nuisance doctrine, not on the character, duration, or regulation of the apartment tenancies themselves.
Possessory injunction over farmland and growing crops between a longtime possessor and an alleged tenant; no letting of dwelling rooms is at issue.

Rent suit on a 19-month lease of the lower half of a duplex; tenant's defense was disturbance by the upstairs co-tenant's noisy household ('moral eviction' doctrine). This is ordinary long-term residential leasing, not short-term room letting or boarding, and the holding concerns landlord warranty, not letting's legal character.
Dispute over whether a piano is exempt from a lessor's privilege/pledge for unpaid rent; a landlord-tenant exemption-statute question with no lodging or boarding arrangement involved.

A father leased a home for his wife and children, who lived there without paying him rent or board; dispute concerns seizure of his daughter's furniture. No paying lodger/boarder arrangement is present -- the daughter is a dependent family beneficiary, not a compensated occupant.

Suit by a landowner against a possessor for revenues collected from a blacksmith's shop that encroached onto plaintiff's lot; a commercial-premises revenue/prescription case, unrelated to residential letting or lodging.
Succession proceeding over the sale of a decedent's 'right of occupancy' of a leased drug-store premises; a commercial lease/succession-accounting dispute, not residential lodging.
Lease-cancellation dispute where national prohibition made a leased 'bar-room' unusable for its purpose; a commercial-premises frustration-of-purpose case, not residential lodging.

Dispute among commercial sublessees (a photography studio and a storekeeper) and their common lessor over floor space and stairway/vestibule appurtenances in a commercial building; no residential lodging or boarding is involved.
